prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1196; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but I understand the adjuster needs it for the file. [Claimant name]

Q: Thank you. Can you describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision occurred?

A: I was driving through a parking lot in Sugar Land, heading toward the exit. Traffic was slow, and I was going maybe ten miles an hour.

Q: What happened next?

A: The other vehicle came around the row from the opposite direction and turned into my lane. We ended up nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, more like a bump, but there was a jolt.

Q: Did either vehicle's airbags deploy?

A: No, nothing deployed. Both cars were drivable, though the front of mine was scraped and the bumper was pushed in a bit.

Q: How are you feeling physically since the collision?

A: My neck is stiff and sore, especially when I turn my head to check mirrors. The pain got worse the next morning. I also have a headache that comes and goes.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or other medical provider for this?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same evening. They diagnosed a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: Are you currently receiving any treatment?

A: I have a follow-up with my primary care doctor next week, and I'm doing some gentle stretching at home. I've missed a couple of days of work because turning and lifting are painful.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I was careful and didn't see the other car coming. I just want my car repaired and my neck to get better.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the statement.
